ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an object A with mass $m_{1}=20\mathrm{kg}$ is suspended by three light ropes, with the junction point at $O$. The rope $O B$ is horizontal, and its end $B$ is connected to a person with mass $m_{2}=60\mathrm{kg}$ placed on a horizontal surface. The rope $O A$ makes an angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction. Both object A and the person are in a state of rest. It is known that $\sin 37^{\circ}=0.6$ and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$. The acceleration due to gravity $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Assume that the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction.

1. What are the magnitudes of the tensions in the light ropes $O A$ and $O B$?
2. What is the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the person? What is its direction?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure, three light ropes are connected at node O: one horizontal rope OB connects from O to the left to a person standing on the horizontal ground; one vertical rope connects from O downward to a suspended object; one inclined rope connects from O to the upper right to an upper support, and the angle between this inclined rope and the vertical direction is marked as θ=37°. In the figure, the person is stationary on the horizontal ground, and the suspended object is also stationary. Then reason: The mass of the suspended object is m1=20 kg, and it is stationary, so the tension in the vertical rope pulling node O downward is equal to its weight: T竖=m1g=20×10=200 N. Perform force equilibrium on node O. Let the tension of the inclined rope OA be T_OA; its angle with the vertical direction is 37°, so the vertical component is T_OA cos37°, and the horizontal component is T_OA sin37°. Equilibrium in the vertical direction gives T_OA cos37°=200 N, so T_OA=200/0.8=250 N. In equilibrium in the horizontal direction, the tension of the horizontal rope OB is equal to the horizontal component of the inclined rope: T_OB=T_OA sin37°=250×0.6=150 N. Analyze the forces on the person: the pulling force of rope OB on the person is along the rope pointing toward O, namely horizontally to the right, with magnitude 150 N. The person is stationary, so the static friction force of the ground on the person must balance this pulling force, with magnitude 150 N and direction horizontally to the left.
